title: Coram
summary: Coram is a Brookhaven hamlet placename on the old country road, with related forms including Moncorum, Corum, Coraway, Puding, Wincoram, and Winecorum.
map_geometry_source: Coram is identified as a Brookhaven farming hamlet near the town center, with nearby Coram Hills also referenced. Point is an approximate modern hamlet-center marker, not a historic boundary.
introduction_content: Coram is a Brookhaven placename tied to the old Middle Country Road and nearby Coram Hills. Moncorum is one early form of the same name rather than a separate place.
history_content: Coram brings together the hamlet name, old country road references, and related historical spellings. Dated road and land records appear in the Historic Timeline with their own sources.
translation_content:
Related forms include Coram, Corum, Moncorum, Wincoram, Winecorum, Coraway, and Puding. The name is interpreted as referring to a valley or low country, likely tied to the landscape near the Coram Hills.

Why Place Names Matter

“Indigenous Peoples’ choice to name and rename is deeply embedded in community-based decisions to reawaken responsibilities, rights, and jurisdiction.”

— Christina Gray and Andrew Ambers, The Rematriation of Indigenous Place Names (2026), Indigenous Laws and Governance
land_loss_content: Coram shows how a Native place-name could be shortened and absorbed into a modern hamlet name while still carrying older topographic meaning. Recording the longer forms helps reconnect the present-day place with the layered record behind it.
whereintheworld_content: The blue marker is approximate and general. It uses the modern Coram hamlet center near Middle Country Road as a public map reference, not an exact historic farm or road-boundary coordinate.
